dedupe_keys.name: agepopdenom fine scale age population model

description: AgePopDenom is an R model for estimating age-specific population surfaces where recent detailed census data are missing. The JOSS paper describes fitting age distributions to household surveys and predicting them over WorldPop grids, with a reported five-kilometre output scale. Its own DESCRIPTION states MIT plus a licence file, and the own licence text is MIT, so the package code is free. Inputs are surveys, gridded population, boundaries and optional spatial covariates. Outputs are modelled age counts by cell. Geographic and temporal coverage follow the supplied surveys and population layers. Infrastructure planners could use age-specific demand estimates in healthcare, evacuation or shelter simulations. A caveat is that sparse surveys and migration can create spatial bias, and small-area estimates must carry uncertainty. WorldPop and survey data have separate rights and access conditions. No directly related catalogue record was confirmed. No population data were downloaded and no fit was run.
name: AgePopDenom fine-scale age population model
notes: G5 G5-0922. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
outputs: Estimated population by single year of age on fine grids
